hints: Take the values one at a time. What are the choices for the first value, and what remains to be decided afterwards?
Either it is in the subset or it is not, and in both cases the same question is asked of the rest of the values.
So the recursion has two branches per value and reaches a complete subset when the values run out. Record a copy of what you have built there.
Keep one working list, appending before one branch and removing after it - that is the backtracking, and it keeps the memory O(n) rather than one list per subset.
